niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand vs. direct response), budget, geography, platform preferences (Roku, Samsung, Fire TV, LG, etc.), and whether you need creative, programmatic buying, or direct-sold premium placements. I can recommend specific agencies if you tell me more, but here’s a concise guide to help you decide plus a shortlist of well-regarded options by type.

Key questions for me
- Are you running brand awareness or performance/conversion campaigns?
- Monthly budget range (rough ballpark)?
- Target geography (US, EMEA, APAC, global)?
- Do you need creative production (30–60s video, dynamic creative)?
- Preferred buying approach: programmatic (DSP) vs. direct deals with platforms?
- Any required measurement/attribution partners (Nielsen, Comscore, MOAT, etc.)?

Types of partners and example names
- Global full-service media agencies (best for large, integrated campaigns and cross-channel measurement): GroupM (MediaCom/Wavemaker/Mindshare), Omnicom Media Group (OMD/PHD), Publicis Media (Starcom/Zenith), Dentsu, Havas.
- Programmatic/tech-forward agencies (strong with DSPs, data, optimization): independent programmatic boutiques or shops that use The Trade Desk, DV360, etc. — many full-service agencies also have strong programmatic teams.
- CTV specialists / performance-first: agencies/platforms that focus heavily on CTV and performance (e.g., MNTN and other CTV-first vendors).
- Creative & ad‑tech partners: Innovid (creative/ad serving), measurement partners like Nielsen, Comscore, TVision, and supply-side partners like Magnite/SpotX for premium inventory.
- Platform-managed solutions: Roku Ads, Samsung Ads, Amazon Ads — they sell directly and also have preferred agency partners.

What to look for when choosing
- Proven case studies for your objective and vertical
- Inventory access (premium direct deals vs. programmatic access to exchanges)
- Measurement & attribution (integration with Nielsen/Comscore/third-party viewability)
- Creative capabilities (dynamic CTV, versioning, interactive units)
- Transparency on fees, media placements, and reporting cadence
- Fraud/pre-bid verification and viewability practices
- Optimization processes and SLAs
- Platform relationships (Roku, Samsung, Amazon, LG, etc.)

Suggested next steps
1. Tell me the answers to the questions above (goal, budget, geography, need for creative).  
2. I’ll recommend 3–5 agencies or platform partners matched to your needs and a short checklist of questions to ask them in an RFP or call.

If you want, give me a brief about your campaign (objective, budget, geography) and I’ll suggest specific agencies to contact.
